Solution 1 is the only candidate with a checkable argument, and its layer-group count holds up.

**Layer groups.** Let ρ: G → Isom(ℝ²) be the projection to the plane. The kernel of ρ consists of elements acting trivially on the plane, so it is trivial or generated by the horizontal mirror σ_h. If σ_h ∈ G, then σ_h is central and G ≅ W × ℤ₂ for the wallpaper group W = ρ(G). If σ_h ∉ G, then G ≅ W. All 17 wallpaper groups occur in the second case (layer groups with no z-action), and all 17 occur in the first case (the "/m" layer groups such as p6/mmm). The 17 wallpaper groups are pairwise non-isomorphic as abstract groups, and W × ℤ₂ has a nontrivial finite normal subgroup while wallpaper groups do not. The W × ℤ₂ are also distinct from one another. This gives 17 + 17 = 34 classes, which matches Solution 1.

Solutions 2 and 3 give 68 and 63 layer classes. Both exceed the 80-group count only slightly, but neither gives any derivation, and Solution 3's count is 17 below the 80 layer groups that the 34 classes already fail to exhaust. Their layer numbers are unsupported, and 68 and 63 are inconsistent with the structure above, which pins the layer count at 34 in the sense that all distinct abstract types are accounted for by W and W × ℤ₂.

**Rod groups.** I could not verify Solution 1's rod count of 32 from first principles. The decomposition into ℤ-type (F ⋊ ℤ, classified by F and an outer automorphism class) and D∞-type (amalgams A *_F B) is the right framework, and the listed families are plausible, but I did not check each of the 75 entries. Solutions 2 and 3 give 61 and 57 with no supporting work. Since Solution 1 is the only one with a structurally correct layer count, it is the best candidate, though its rod component is unconfirmed.

Solution 1's text has a stray "wait, recording" phrase, but that does not change its answer.

CHOICE: 1
